results.title: Reassessing weights in large-scale assessments and ...
results.content: Given these complexities, there is a need for simulation studies that explore different sampling structures and research questions, such as how to incorporate sampling weights into MLMs. While TIMSS and other LSAs recommend the use of sampling weights, they offer limited guidance on when and how to apply these weights in multilevel models. Within a complex sampling framework, TIMSS employs a total student sampling weight that combines selection probabilities across three hierarchical levels: school, class, and student (LaRoche et al., 2020. In our simulation study to test the informativeness of weights, we analyzed the power of two tests, DuMouchel and Duncan (DD) and Pfeffermann and Sverchkov (PS), under different conditions involving classroom sampling (CS), student nonresponse (NR STU), and school nonresponse (NR SCH). Based on our simulation results, which uses sampling techniques employed by LSAs, and an applied example using the TIMSS Germany dataset, we recommend that researchers test if model weights can be considered informative using both the DD and PS tests.
